security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode code writes to mstatus fields (MIE/MPIE/TVM/TW/TSR/MPRV/MXR/SUM) that the spec requires to be writable, but the underlying hardware implementation incorrectly implements them as read-only (WARL hardwired to 0 or constant), causing the CSR write to be silently ignored.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_write|csr_set|csr_clear\s+CSR_MSTATUS.*(MIE|MPIE|TVM|TW|TSR|MPRV|MXR|SUM).*(?<!followed by csr_read to verify the write took effect)
security_spec.summary: Spec now mandates that MIE/MPIE/TVM/TW/TSR/MPRV/MXR/SUM bits must be writable under defined conditions; OpenSBI relies on these writes taking effect — if hardware silently ignores writes to these fields, M-mode interrupt gating (MIE), S-mode trap interception (TVM/TW/TSR), or memory-access emulation (MPRV/MXR/SUM) silently break without detection, leading to privilege enforcement gaps or unhandled traps.

findings.finding: Writes MPIE=0 to CSR_MSTATUS (line 796) without subsequent csr_read verification. MPIE is in the spec's list of vulnerable WARL fields. If hardware incorrectly hardwires MPIE to 1 (read-only), MRET would enable interrupts (MIE ← MPIE) after the mode switch, leaving S-mode entered with interrupts unexpectedly enabled.

Sets MSTATUS_MPRV via csrrs to perform unprivileged loads/stores, then restores via csrw. No verification read checks that MPRV actually took effect. If MPRV is hardwired to 0, the access silently runs with M-mode privileges, and the emulation layer misinterprets the result (no fault when one should have occurred). Used by all sbi_load_*/sbi_store_* helpers.

Sets MSTATUS_MPRV | MSTATUS_MXR via csrrs to fetch instructions from S/U-mode pages (MXR makes read-only execute pages readable). Same pattern as above—no read-back to verify MPRV and MXR took effect. If MXR is hardwired to 0, instruction fetches from execute-only pages would incorrectly fault.

Identical MPRV set/restore pattern as sbi_unpriv.c (csrrs to set MPRV, csrw to restore). Used for LR/SC emulation. Same risk: if MPRV is hardwired to 0, LR/SC emulation silently operates with M-mode privileges, potentially missing access faults or guest-page faults.

Clears MSTATUS_MPRV via csrc (lines 27, 45) inside trap handlers that fire when MPRV-mediated unprivileged accesses trap. This is a safety-critical path; clearing MPRV prevents recursive traps. Since csrc atomically clears the bit, and a hardware-level MPRV==0 means the csrc is a no-op, no read-back is needed.
findings.snippet:
li a4, MSTATUS_MPRV
csrc CSR_MSTATUS, a4

findings.finding: Restores entire mstatus/mstatush from trap frame on trap exit. The restored value was previously read from hardware CSR (via TRAP_SAVE_INFO on trap entry), so any WARL effects are already baked into the saved value. Writes all mstatus fields but using a previously-read snapshot—no verification needed since the write is semantically restoring prior hardware state.
findings.snippet:
REG_L t0, SBI_TRAP_REGS_OFFSET(mstatus)(a0)
csrw CSR_MSTATUS, t0

findings.finding: Writes only MSTATUS_FS and MSTATUS_VS based on misa checks (lines 41-46). Neither FS nor VS are in the spec's vulnerable-field list (MIE/MPIE/TVM/TW/TSR/MPRV/MXR/SUM). The code guards writes behind misa interrogation, so it never sets FS/VS on hardware lacking those extensions.

Clears MSTATUS_MDT (or MSTATUSH_MDT on RV32) via csrc. MDT is an M-mode-only control bit, not in the spec's vulnerable-field list. Used at cold boot, warm boot, and trap save points—all appropriate locations.

Writes MSTATUSH_MPV on RV32 (line 800-801) for hypervisor extension support. MPV is not in the spec's vulnerable-field list. The value is part of a read-modify-write sequence that includes a prior csr_read(CSR_MSTATUSH) at line 799.
